01The reason

Why I run four copies of the same indicator

One copy of Levl Up gives you two higher timeframes: HTF and HTF². Two things I want do not fit into two slots, so I run four copies.

Reason 1 — I want 1h closures at 4h key levels

On a 5m chart, Auto gives me HTF = 1h and HTF² = daily. Both slots are taken. There is no third slot for 4h.

So the 4h layer needs its own copy. That copy watches 4h and nothing else, which also means it can never report the same closure as the first one.

Reason 2 — I do not want to see monthly

On a 1h chart, Auto gives HTF = daily and HTF² = monthly. I want the daily alignment. Monthly does not interest me and I do not want it on the chart.

Switching off the HTF² toggles removes monthly, but that also gives up the second slot, and I still want 4h key levels visible on the 1h chart. So the 1h chart gets two copies of its own: one that stays aligned with daily and has monthly switched off, and one that puts the 4h levels back on top.

The result 4 copies, 3 alerts. Copy 1 plots on every chart except the 1h and carries two of the alerts. Copy 2 sits on the 5m and carries the third. Copies 3 and 4 belong to the 1h chart and never alert.
02The mechanics

Three things Levl Up does that make this possibleUnderstand these and the four copies stop looking random

1 — Custom TF Alignment only activates on the matching chart

In Closure Formation → TF Alignment you pick Auto or Custom. Custom has two fields: the chart timeframe the mapping applies to (left) and the HTF to use (right).

Custom only applies when your chart timeframe matches the left field. Set it to 1 hour → 4 hours and the same copy behaves two ways:

  • On a 5m chart the chart is not 1h, so the mapping does not apply and the copy runs on standard alignment. HTF = 1h, HTF² = 4h.
  • On a 1h chart the chart matches, the mapping applies. HTF = 4h.

That is how copy 2 gets 4h onto the 5m chart and copy 4 gets 4h onto the 1h chart, from the same setting.

2 — A display toggle is also a key level switch

The Key Level Filter only counts a level type whose display toggle is on. Switch off HTF Swings and the filter stops seeing HTF swings entirely. Same for HTF² Swings, HTF FVG, HTF² FVG, PDH/PDL and PWH/PWL.

Applied Copy 1: HTF Swings on + HTF² Swings on → watches 1h and daily.
Copy 2: HTF Swings off + HTF² Swings on → watches 4h only.
The two sets do not overlap, so one closure can never fire both alerts.

3 — The Visibility tab separates the copies per chart

Four copies means four copies on every chart. The Visibility tab controls which chart timeframes a copy is allowed to draw on.

  • Minutes 5 – 5 → only on the 5m chart.
  • Hours 1 – 1 → only on the 1h chart.
  • Hours 4 – 24 with everything else on → everywhere except 1h.

The SMT peers: I trade NQ and compare it against ES. YM does not interest me. If you trade something else, put your own assets into the two peer fields.

Use the named zone, not the offset The timezone list has two kinds of entry. Named zones like America/New_York follow daylight saving. Fixed offsets like UTC-4 do not.

I ran UTC-4 for a long time and it is correct in summer only. When the clocks change, every session window shifts by an hour and the alerts fire an hour early or late until you notice and fix it by hand. If you run session-filtered alerts, pick America/New_York and it takes care of itself.

2 · from 5m and 3m

Why Auto and not Custom: Auto shifts the higher timeframes down with the chart, so the same configuration works on every timeframe I open. On 5m it gives HTF = 1h and HTF² = daily. On 3m it gives HTF = 30m and HTF² = 4h.

The 5m and 3m are only about the alerts. To alert on a candle closure you have to create the alert from a lower timeframe. I trade the 1h during London, so that alert gets created on the 5m. I trade the 30m during NY AM, so that one gets created on the 3m. The copy itself keeps plotting on every other chart regardless.

Why HTF and HTF² Swings and FVGs are both on: that is what puts 1h and daily into the key level set. Together with PDH/PDL and PWH/PWL, those are the levels this copy watches.

The two alarm screenshots Same copy, two states. London for the 5m alert, NY AM for the 3m alert. You set one, create the alert, then set the other and create the second alert. Section 08 has the order.

The alert events

The events I have on are the ones that give me my entry alert. Sweep, FVG Touch and Swing Breach are off because the Key Level Filter is on, and a formation can only form at a key level anyway. Those extra events would not tell me anything the closure and CISD events do not already tell me.

How it gets to 4h: Custom is set to 1 hour → 4 hours, but the chart is 5m, so the mapping does not apply to the chart itself and the copy runs on standard alignment. 08Alerts

Creating the three alertsOrder matters

TradingView freezes your indicator settings the moment you create an alert. Change a setting afterwards and the running alert does not change with it. That is what lets instance 1 produce two different alerts from one copy.

Alert 1 — London, 5m, levels 1h + daily

  • Open the 5m chart.
  • On instance 1: London on, NY AM off.
  • Right click the chart → Add alert. Condition = Levl Up → Any alert() function call.
  • Trigger = Once per bar.
  • Name it LDN 5m · 1h+D, so you can tell the three apart later.
Where the name field is It is not on the main alert screen. Click the Message button in the alert dialog and the Alert name field is at the top of the Edit message screen that opens. That name is what shows up in the alert manager, in the toast and in the alert log. Worth doing: three alerts that are all called "Levl Up" tell you nothing when one fires.

Alert 2 — London, 5m, level 4h

  • Same 5m chart, but create it on instance 2.
  • Same options. Name: LDN 5m · 4h.

Alert 3 — NY AM, 3m, levels 30m + 4h

  • Switch the chart to 3m. Standard alignment now reads HTF = 30m and HTF² = 4h by itself.
  • Back into instance 1: NY AM on, London off.
  • Create the alert. Name: NY 3m · 30m+4h.
  • Then set instance 1 back to London on, NY AM off. Both alerts keep running with the settings they were created with.
Five minute overlap My London window ends at 08:05 and NY AM starts at 08:00. Both alerts come from instance 1 with the PD/PW breaks on, so a break inside those five minutes sends two notifications. I leave it, the odds are small enough. If you want it clean, end London at 08:00.

Instances 3 and 4 get no alert. They are drawing layers for the 1h chart.

10Templates

Save it as an indicator templateThe step most people skip

Once the four copies are configured, open the indicator dropdown on your chart toolbar and hit Save indicator template. Give it a name. TradingView stores all four copies with all their settings as one entry.

Why this matters

  • Runtime errors. If an indicator drops out with a runtime error, you do not rebuild anything. Pick the template and it adds the copy back, fully configured.
  • Bias variants. I keep one template per bias state, so switching is one click instead of four dialogs.
  • Different assets. If you run SMT on Custom and trade more than one market, save a template per market with the right peers in the fields.
TemplateWhat it is
AutoBias set to Auto · Levl Up x 4
LongBias set to Bullish · Levl Up x 4
ShortBias set to Bearish · Levl Up x 4
NeutralBias set to Neutral · Levl Up x 4
CleanEvery indicator removed

Everything else in the four copies stays identical across the templates. Only the Bias setting changes.

11Notes

Before you copy this

  • This is built around how I trade. London on the 1h, NY AM on the 30m, NQ against ES. The structure works for other setups, the numbers in it will not.
  • Change the SMT peers if you trade something else. An uncorrelated peer produces divergence that means nothing.
  • Take the named timezone. A fixed offset like UTC-4 does not follow daylight saving, and your session windows drift by an hour when the clocks change. America/New_York handles it.
  • Build the copies in order. Finish instance 1, then add the indicator again and adjust from there. Configuring four at once is how you lose track of which one you are editing.
  • Alerts are frozen at creation. If you change a setting that should affect an alert, delete the alert and create it again. Editing the indicator does not update it.
  • Save the template when you are done. See section 10.
The principle underneath all of it One copy watches one set of levels. Everything in this document is that rule applied four times.
12Reference

What every setting doesPanel by panel, so you can read the screenshots

This is the function of each setting, not my reason for using it. If a screenshot leaves you wondering what a checkbox actually changes, it is in here.

General

Label Size
Size of every text label on the chart. Keep it small when several copies run at once.
Timezone
Display timezone for candle time labels and for the alert session windows. Named zones (America/New_York and the like) follow daylight saving, fixed offsets (UTC-4) do not.
Bias
The master directional filter, deciding which formations show. Neutral shows both directions, Bullish and Bearish only one, Auto derives bias from daily structure and updates live.
Show Bias Display
On-chart readout of the current bias.
ADR
Average Daily Range over 20 days plus how much of it price has used today. Context for whether a move is already extended.

Closure Formation

History
How many past formations to keep per type. Low for live trading, high for studying history.
Backtest
Keeps invalidated formations on the chart so you can study how they played out.
TF Alignment
How the higher timeframe is chosen. Auto uses standard Fractal-Model alignment. Custom lets you set it: field 1 is the chart TF the mapping applies to, field 2 is the HTF to use.
Closure Formation
The main break line at the closure level. This one toggle controls the whole standard formation, because break line, CISD, continuation and projection are a single object.
CISD
Change in State of Delivery line. The confirmation trigger that makes a formation valid.
Pending CISD
The next potential CISD level, and where it would form.
Continuation CISD
After a valid closure, price should continue and form a continuation CISD. That is an entry opportunity.
Protected Swings
The levels a move defends on its way. The CISD marks where the move started, Protected Swings marks what it has been protecting since, drawn as a staircase rather than a single anchor.
SMT CISD
A CISD that also confirms an SMT divergence. Trigger plus divergence in one.
CTF Closure Formation
Candle closure on the chart timeframe itself, for trading directly on a higher TF. Only on 15m charts and above.
Draw only at Key Levels
Draws a closure formation only when it forms at a key level. Hidden formations are not deleted, they return when you switch it off. SMT formations always show.

Additional

PDH / PDL
Previous day high and low.
PWH / PWL
Previous week high and low.
EQ
The 50% midpoint of the relevant range. Both, HTF only or chart only, with a Latest-only option.
HTF Swings
Significant swing highs and lows on the HTF, with a Max count.
HTF² Swings
Swings one level higher, the HTF of your HTF. On a 5m chart HTF is 1h so HTF² is daily. On a 1h chart HTF is daily so HTF² is monthly. With TF Alignment on Custom, HTF² follows your mapping.
CTF Swings
The same on your chart timeframe.
Separator
Vertical lines where each HTF period begins.
Line 1 / 2 / 3
Three session lines marking the opening price at a time of day, entered as HH:MM in New York time. Defaults 18:00, 09:30 and 10:00. Cleared at the day rollover, never carried over.
Fib Projection
Fibonacci targets projected from a valid formation's CISD range, as objective take-profit zones.
T-Spot / EQ Fill
Highlights a reaction zone inside the formation, after a valid C2 or C3 closure.

FVG

CTF FVG
Fair value gaps on the chart timeframe, with colors, a Max count and an invalidation mode.
HTF FVG
The same on the HTF.
HTF² FVG
Gaps two levels up. A daily gap drawn on your 5m chart is a bigger magnet than a 1h one.
iFVG
When a regular FVG is fully traded through it can invert, support and resistance flipping. The Max TF dropdown limits where it appears.
Bias Filter
Hides FVGs pointing against the current bias, so you only see gaps matching your direction.
Stop extending after touch · Bars
Stops an FVG box growing to the right, this many candles after price first trades into it, so old gaps do not stretch across the screen. Counted in the gap's own timeframe. It does not change when the gap dies.
Max
Controls what is drawn, not what is tracked. The indicator remembers up to 3× your Max per direction and the Key Level Filter checks all of them, so a formation can qualify through a gap you can no longer see.

Key Level Filter — the logic worth reading twice

Two independent toggles use the same mark. Draw only at Key Levels (Closure Formation group) controls what is drawn. Key Level Filter (Alarm Filter group) controls what alerts. They do not affect each other.

  • What counts as a key level: HTF and HTF² swing highs and lows, PDH/PDL and PWH/PWL, HTF and HTF² FVGs.
  • What deliberately does not: CTF swings, CTF FVGs, iFVGs, EQ and session lines. Chart-timeframe levels sit too close to price, so almost every formation would qualify and the filter would filter nothing.
  • How a formation earns the mark: when price breaks or trades into a key level, a 3-HTF-candle window opens. A formation only counts if it confirms inside that window. Direction matters, and each level triggers only once.
  • The part most people miss: the filter only counts a level type whose display toggle is on. Switch off HTF² FVG and no formation ever qualifies through an HTF² gap. This is the main lever, and it is what makes the four copies in this document work.
  • Exception: SMT formations always pass both filters. The divergence is their own confluence.

SMT & PSP

Show SMT
Master switch for all SMT features. Off means all SMT off.
HTF SMT · CTF SMT
Divergence at HTF swing points and at chart-timeframe swing points.
CTF SMT History
How many CTF divergences to keep on screen per side.
PDH/PDL SMT · PWH/PWL SMT
Divergence at the previous day and previous week highs and lows.
SMT on HTF Candle
Draws divergence on the HTF candle boxes.
Asset Label
Writes the diverging peer's name on the divergence line, so you see which instrument failed to follow.
SMT Mode
The instruments you are compared against. Automatic recognises your instrument and uses two correlated peers (NQ → ES + YM). Custom lets you set the peers yourself.
Enable Second SMT
Custom only. Off compares against a single peer, which is slightly lighter since the second symbol is no longer fetched.
Peer 1 · Peer 2 · Inverse
Your two peer symbols in Custom mode. Inverse is for instruments that move opposite to yours, such as DXY, so the divergence still reads correctly.
PSP
Precision Swing Point. Compares closing direction candle by candle: you close up, a peer closes down. Require C2 and Require SMT narrow it further.

HTF Candles

Show HTF Candles
Draws HTF candles as boxes beside your chart, so you read HTF structure without leaving your timeframe.
Count / Offset
How many candles, and how far right they sit.
Time labels
Adapts to the timeframe: HH:mm intraday, day name daily, month monthly.
Second HTF Box
A second, higher-TF set alongside the first, for example 1h and 4h boxes together. Own toggle and TF field.
HTF Info Label
Timeframe plus a live countdown to candle close on the live box.

Alarm Filter

Key Level Filter
Formation alerts (Sweep, C2 Closure, C3 Closure, CISD, CISD Touch, Continuation CISD) only fire when the formation is at a key level. Level alerts such as FVG Touch, Swing Breach and PD/PW breaks are untouched by it.
Session Filter
Master toggle. Alerts only fire during the enabled sessions.
Asia / London / NY AM / NY PM
Four sessions, each with a toggle and a time window. Times use the General-group timezone.
HTF Sweep
Fires when the HTF sweeps a level.
HTF C2 / C3 Closure
Fires when the second or third candle of the formation closes.
CISD
Fires when the confirmation trigger fires.
CISD Touch
Fires when price touches a pending CISD, so you can get ready before confirmation.
Continuation CISD
Fires on the continuation entry after a valid closure.
PDH/PDL · PWH/PWL Break
Fires when previous day or previous week liquidity is taken.
FVG Touch · Swing Breach
Level events for CTF, HTF and HTF². The HTF² ones only work while the matching HTF² display toggle is on, since the indicator only tracks what it shows.
Alerting on a closure To alert on a candle closure, create the alert from a lower timeframe. For a 1h closure use 5m, for a 30m closure use 3m. That is why both my alert charts are lower than the timeframe I actually trade.

Visibility tab

Ticks · Seconds · Minutes · Hours · Days · Weeks · Months · Ranges
Each chart timeframe class has a checkbox and a from–to range. The copy only draws on charts inside an enabled range. This is what keeps four copies from all appearing on the same chart.
